title: Unfinished Seal — proposal
open: Can we design a cryptographic seal that is valid only when every named institution jointly authorizes the same artifact, ceremony identifier, and expiry?
status: Withdrawal, missing assent, and replay still need exact semantics; the certificate establishes digital participation, not sincerity or physical presence. Related directions include distributed key generation and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A certificate is valid if and only if it carries every named institution's fresh authorization of the same artifact, ceremony identifier, and expiry, with exact semantics for withdrawal, missing assent, and replay.
why: It enables shared civic symbols whose authenticated creation requires a genuinely cooperative act, rather than unilateral issuance.

title: Unattributed Veto Liturgy — proposal
open: Can institutions with mutually incompatible private constraints jointly compute an acceptable shared ceremony without revealing those constraints? Each institution submits private predicates over an agreed vocabulary of gestures and utterances, and the parties wish to release either one acceptable ceremony or a single failure symbol and nothing else.
status: Theological acceptability is formalized through agreed predicates, but a key obstacle remains: repeated feasibility queries can expose another institution's taboos. The record points to SPDZ and collaborative proofs over distributed witnesses as relevant techniques, but no protocol for this setting is given.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the only output is either a single ceremony satisfying all institutions' private acceptability predicates over the agreed vocabulary, or one failure symbol; in particular, repeated feasibility queries must not leak any institution's taboos or private constraints beyond what the output itself reveals.
why: It would let incompatible traditions hold joint rites without private boundaries becoming bargaining ammunition; without such guarantees, the act of negotiating a shared liturgy itself exposes what each side holds sacred.
key_works: SPDZ; collaborative proofs over distributed witnesses.

title: Chorus Without a Master — proposal
open: Can a group of parties, each holding a private musical motif, jointly produce a common choral score without any single party learning the others' motifs, such that the score satisfies contribution, duration, and balance rules and its public performance counts as an explicitly authorized disclosure?
status: This is a proposal; no protocol exists yet. Local parts may imply other parts, and motif extraction, covert messages, and rehearsal metadata require analysis. Related directions include private-output MPC and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which private motifs yield a common score meeting the contribution, duration, and balance rules, with the eventual performance realized as an authorized disclosure — and with analysis covering the facts that local parts may imply other parts, and that motif extraction, covert messages, and rehearsal metadata are accounted for.
why: It would yield a cultural work whose first complete public realization requires cooperation — no single party can perform it alone.

title: Reciprocal Silence — proposal
open: Can a set of participants holding anonymous credentials prove that an approved quorum of them jointly observed a communal silence — satisfying an agreed acoustic predicate — while revealing nothing to the computing institutions beyond a single completion bit? More precisely, no raw audio and no record of which individuals attended may ever be submitted to, or reconstructable by, the parties performing the computation.
status: This is currently only a proposal. Existing sensor signatures establish provenance of readings but do not guarantee truthful measurement, and anonymity is known to fail against cameras, small quorums, and known attendance. Related building blocks are Coconut credentials and Prio's validated private aggregation.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which an anonymous quorum, approved via credentials, jointly evaluates an acoustic predicate over their audio inputs and outputs only one completion bit, with the computing institutions learning neither the raw audio nor individual attendance; the construction should remain secure against the known deanonymization avenues (cameras, small quorums, known attendance) rather than assuming them away.
why: It would let communities hold joint mourning or silence observances that require verifying a quorum actually participated, without forcing members onto a shared attendee register.
key_works: Coconut credentials; Prio’s validated private aggregation.

title: Many Tongues, One Oath — proposal
open: Can several institutions, each holding a privately worded oath in its own religious or historical vocabulary, jointly compute a public certificate that their wordings express one and the same formal obligation? Formally, each institution supplies private wording plus an approved translation into a common obligation schema, and the parties run a joint computation whose public output certifies equality of the translated obligations.
status: No protocol or construction is on record. The translation's legitimacy remains a human agreement; cryptography cannot prove unrestricted semantic equivalence, so only the equality of translated obligations is in scope, not the fidelity of the translations themselves. Related machinery consists of collaborative zk-SNARKs over distributed private inputs.
solved_when: A multiparty protocol (of the collaborative zk-SNARK type over distributed private inputs) exists in which each institution's private wording and approved translation remain hidden, while the public output certifies that all translated obligations are equal under the common formal schema.
why: It would let communities with distinct religious and historical vocabularies enter shared operational commitments without abandoning their own wording — the binding content is certified common even though the expressions remain private and diverse.
key_works: Collaborative zk-SNARKs over distributed private inputs.

title: Withdrawable Communion — proposal
open: Can a jointly computable ritual be made *withdrawable* — completing only when the set of participants whose consent is current and unrevoked still satisfies every required community quorum — while keeping the set of withdrawers entirely hidden from the output?
status: No construction is known. Known obstructions: timing, compromised devices, or nearly known quorums can expose a withdrawal, and secret consent cannot prove freedom from physical coercion. Related primitives include Coconut and malicious MPC over private state.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the ritual completes exactly when all required quorum conditions hold over currently consenting, unrevoked participants, no information about who withdrew is released, and the known failure channels — timing leakage, compromised devices, and inference from nearly known quorums — are addressed.
why: It would give collective ceremonies digital legitimacy that still contains an enforceable individual right to leave, something ordinary consent or quorum mechanisms cannot provide.
key_works: Coconut; malicious MPC over private state.

title: No-Humiliation Ceremony — proposal
open: Can a group of participants jointly compute a ceremony that everyone finds acceptable, without any individual being forced to reveal which parts are costly or humiliating to them? Formally, is there a mechanism that truthfully elicits each participant's burdens and benefit thresholds while preserving privacy and voluntary participation?
status: Currently, actors can exaggerate their burdens. The missing mechanism-design result is truthful elicitation compatible with privacy and voluntary participation; related efforts include MPC implementations of private economic mechanisms.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which the computed ceremony respects every submitted burden cap and meets each participant's declared minimum benefit, with truthful elicitation (no participant gains by exaggerating burdens), privacy of individual inputs, and voluntary participation.
why: It would allow groups to cooperate on shared rituals without anyone having to publicly admit which gestures feel humiliating or costly, removing a major barrier to collective participation.
key_works: MPC implementations of private economic mechanisms.

title: Indispensable Hand — proposal
open: Can a set of parties jointly compute a "ritual" output such that no role's contribution can be dispensed with — specifically, when each honest role holds an independently sampled hidden seed, can it be guaranteed that all other roles together cannot predict the canonical session digest before that role's authorized contribution?
status: Binding a seed does not prove its entropy or prevent voluntary disclosure; adaptive inputs and abort selection currently require a contributiveness reduction that is not yet established. Related areas are distributed key generation and adversarial coin-flipping limits.
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility result) exists for rituals computable only jointly, together with a contributiveness reduction handling adaptive inputs and abort selection, establishing that binding a seed entails unpredictability of the digest prior to its authorized contribution.
why: It would give rituals with a precise, provable property of indispensable cooperation, ruling out degenerate instantiations where a bound seed is voluntarily disclosed or lacks entropy.
key_works: Distributed key generation; adversarial coin-flipping limits.

title: Answerless Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a national census be collected so that respondents secret-share their answers directly from their own devices, with institutions receiving only a fixed collection of privacy-protected statistics? In other words, can the entire census pipeline be designed so that no institution ever holds individuals' raw answers, yet the published aggregates are jointly computable and auditable?
status: The proposal builds on Prio-style secret-sharing and differential privacy, but compromised devices, fraudulent enrollment, and coercive collection remain unresolved, and exact tiny-cell outputs can still reveal individual responses.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which respondents secret-share answers from their own devices, institutions receive only a fixed collection of privacy-protected statistics, and the design addresses compromised devices, fraudulent enrollment, coercive collection, and tiny-cell leakage from exact outputs.
why: It would allow a census to be jointly audited by rival institutions without turning any of them into a repository of vulnerable people's answers.

title: Minority Need Without a Roll — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a service provider, for a predeclared region, issue a privacy-protected decision about whether demand for an accommodation is sufficient, without ever seeing a roll of who needs it or the exact prevalence of need?
status: Exact thresholds are known to conflict with strong individual privacy, so any workable scheme must allow service policy to tolerate calibrated uncertainty near the threshold. Related techniques include Prio aggregation and differentially private query release.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that outputs a sufficiency decision for any predeclared region while withholding individual names and exact prevalence counts, and the residual uncertainty near the decision threshold is explicitly calibrated.
why: It would let governments and services grant language, accessibility, or worship accommodations without exposing the very people who need them.
key_works: Prio aggregation; differentially private query release.

title: Many Registers, One Person — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a set of institutions, each holding its own population register, jointly compute deduplicated statistics about the underlying people without any institution learning which records across registers refer to the same person, and without anyone obtaining the merged roster? Formally, the task is to compute aggregate statistics over the union of persons (not records) while hiding record-level linkage and the consolidated identity list from all parties.
status: Aliases, missing documents, and uncertain identity matches are substantive open problems in this setting; ambiguous matches are known to require bounds rather than equality-as-proof of personhood. Related technical foundations include malicious-model MPC and validated private aggregation.
solved_when: A protocol exists that outputs correct deduplicated population statistics while keeping record matches and the merged roster hidden from every institution; where identity matches are ambiguous, the output must give bounds rather than treating equality as proof of personhood.
why: Censuses must often be assembled across disputed administrations, refugee agencies, and overlapping service systems — settings where no single institution can be trusted with the linkage of individuals across registers.

title: No-Trajectory Population Clock — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a sequence of coarse population snapshots be published over time under a fixed privacy budget while revealing nothing about any individual's arrivals, departures, locations, or cross-epoch linkages — even when releases are composed across a lifetime? Formally, this asks for a unified privacy model covering renewal, repeated windows, and lifelong composition in population monitoring.
status: Individually modest releases can collectively expose trajectories, and no unified privacy model yet handles renewal, repeated windows, and lifelong composition together. Related ideas appear in Coconut and in differential privacy for streams.
solved_when: A published mechanism and privacy accounting exist for repeated population releases under an explicit budget, with guarantees covering renewal, repeated windows, and lifelong composition across epochs.
why: It would enable planning for mobile or displaced populations in settings lacking an institutional movement register, where no single authority tracks individuals' trajectories.

title: Protected Nonresponse Audit — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a statistical agency audit response coverage across approved coarse strata while releasing only uncertainty intervals — never any list or identification of nonrespondents? Formally, design a procedure that estimates per-stratum nonresponse rates with valid confidence statements, in a setting where the collector itself may be hostile.
status: Current coverage models rest on assumptions about sampling and dependence among frames, and these assumptions fail against hostile collectors who can coordinate omissions or fabricate apparently independent frames. Related machinery exists in Prio's statistical computation and in differential privacy, but no robust audit procedure of this kind is established.
solved_when: A procedure exists that yields calibrated uncertainty intervals for coverage and nonresponse in each approved coarse stratum, robust to coordinated omissions or fabricated "independent" frames by a hostile collector, and whose outputs do not make nonrespondents easier to target.
why: It would provide evidence of systematic undercounting without handing adversaries a tool to identify or target nonrespondents — the central tension between auditability and protection in censuses without institutional access to individual answers.

title: Disagreement-Preserving Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can competing institutions — each committed to its own finite classification rule for the same population — jointly obtain a privacy-protected census that reports statistical ranges across all of their rules, while no institution ever sees an individual's label under any other rule?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The core obstacle is that arbitrary recodings of the released data can function as identifying queries, so the taxonomy family and its joint sensitivity must be fixed before any responses arrive.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which institutions commit to their classification rules in advance, the census releases differentially private statistical ranges over the full family of rules, and no individual-level answer is disclosed to any institution or released publicly.
why: Service planning must proceed even when institutions disagree about how language, affiliation, ethnicity, or jurisdiction should be classified, so statistics usable by all sides can be published without exposing anyone's individual answer.

title: Betrayal-Bounded Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can a census collect useful population statistics when each respondent locally randomizes their answer before submitting it, so that no institution ever sees a truthful individual response — and how accurate can the resulting aggregate statistics be?
status: Local privacy reduces accuracy and requires trustworthy respondent randomness; unlimited repeated reports consume the guarantee, and outside knowledge remains a limitation. Key works include Warner's randomized response, Prio, and differential privacy.
solved_when: A scheme is specified in which stored reports reveal only locally private observations, together with an analysis of the accuracy loss relative to non-private collection and of how the guarantee degrades under unlimited repeated reports and auxiliary outside knowledge.
why: It would provide census confidentiality that does not rest entirely on permanent institutional trustworthiness or independence, protecting respondents even if all stored reports are later reconstructed.
key_works: Warner’s randomized response; Prio; differential privacy.

title: Household Without a Head — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Can members of a household independently submit their own attributes and co-residence claims, so that the released output is a privacy-protected household distribution computed without any combined form? Formally, the challenge is to design such a protocol in the absence of institutional access to individual answers.
status: Malicious relationship claims alter graph sensitivity. The construction needs a bounded-household model and a workable correction process.
solved_when: A bounded-household model is specified and a workable correction process exists, so that malicious relationship claims cannot unboundedly alter graph sensitivity, and the released distribution is privacy-protected.
why: It would allow census participation that preserves individual agency inside families and shared accommodation.

title: Winner Without a Tally — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election be run so that the only information ever published is the winning candidate (or a prescribed no-result symbol), under a fixed plurality rule and tie-breaker — with no tally, margins, or per-candidate counts ever revealed?
status: This is a proposal; no such protocol is established. Enrollment, voter intent, coercion resistance, and receipt-free inclusion remain separate open issues, and it is known that public ballots plus the winner can still reveal additional information. Related work includes Civitas and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A protocol exists that, under a fixed plurality rule and tie-breaker, outputs only the winner or the prescribed no-result symbol, and leaks nothing beyond that outcome.
why: It would allow leadership selection without disclosing factional strength or defeat margins.

title: Sealed Elimination Election — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can we run a preferential (e.g., instant-runoff or single-transferable-vote) election so that nothing is published except the final winner — with intermediate tallies, transfer patterns, ballot-exhaustion counts, and the candidate elimination order all kept secret?
status: The problem is currently a proposal with no solution known; the stated constraints are that timing and proof shape must not leak the round structure, and fractional transfers must use exact arithmetic. Related lines of work include private voting systems and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists that outputs only the winning candidate, revealing no intermediate tallies, transfer patterns, exhaustion counts, or elimination order; its timing and proof shape do not expose the number of counting rounds; and fractional transfer rules are computed with exact arithmetic rather than implementation-dependent floating point.
why: It would let a group aggregate preferences — for governance, hiring, or ranked choices — without publishing fragile coalition relationships that intermediate counting data would expose.

title: Cross-Community Mandate — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election be run so that the winning candidate takes office only when hidden, membership-linked ballots meet agreed support floors, without exposing who belongs to which community? More precisely: elect the rule-selected candidate while revealing only the authorized outcome — the membership structure and individual ballots stay hidden, and only the aggregate floor conditions are checked.
status: Membership certification is treated as a constitutional choice. It is known that strategic candidate sets and repeated elections can reveal hidden support even when each individual transcript is private, so per-election privacy alone is insufficient. Key works: Coconut; verifiable private voting.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the rule-selected candidate is elected exactly when the hidden membership-linked ballots satisfy the agreed support floors, and no transcript or sequence of elections leaks hidden support beyond the authorized outcome.
why: It would enable power-sharing elections without requiring sectarian electoral maps, letting communities guarantee representation through private support floors rather than gerrymandered districts.

title: Hidden-Turnout Mandate — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election be decided so that the public learns only whether valid participation reached the quorum — the winner if it did, a prescribed no-result symbol if it did not — while exact turnout figures and precinct-level breakdowns remain hidden?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. Polling observation and network traffic may reveal participation, and the quorum result itself necessarily conveys threshold information, so both leakage channels must be confronted. Related tools include Civitas and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A released election protocol outputs the winner whenever valid participation meets the quorum and the no-result symbol otherwise, with exact turnout and precinct breakdowns withheld, and no adversary observing polling or network traffic can recover them.
why: It would let institutions enforce participation requirements without exposing abstention patterns, which can themselves be sensitive information about a community.

title: Marginless Recount — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can a frozen, certified election be recomputed by untrusted parties so that the only information released is either confirmation of the certified winner or a verdict that the record is internally inconsistent? Formally: an audit computation over the frozen ballot data whose sole public outputs are the winner-confirmation bit and an inconsistency flag, leaking nothing else about individual ballots or tally details.
status: Currently, agreement between independent implementations is the available evidence, but this does not prove voter intent: shared bugs, common preprocessing, and common input-validation errors can persist across agreeing implementations. Related work includes collaborative proofs and end-to-end verifiable voting, but no protocol with the marginless, single-outcome disclosure property described here is established in the record.
solved_when: A protocol exists that recomputes the election outcome from the frozen record and outputs only (i) confirmation that the certified winner matches the recomputation, or (ii) an inconsistency verdict, while provably leaking no additional information about voter intent; agreement between independent implementations must additionally rule out shared bugs, common preprocessing, and common input-validation errors as sources of false confirmation.
why: It creates a meaningful computational audit challenge for untrusted recomputation without requiring — or revealing — population-level intelligence about how voters actually voted, closing the gap where implementation agreement alone cannot prove voter intent was honored.

title: Unexposed Nomination — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election be run over a public universe of eligible people in which only those nominees who privately authenticate and consent are actually considered, and in which nothing is revealed beyond the winner?
status: Currently no full solution is described; the record notes that large candidate universes make the approach burdensome, that the announced winner itself constrains the hidden nomination set, and that communications with nominees may expose their choices. Related primitives include Coconut and malicious-secure MPC.
solved_when: A voting scheme is specified in which voters rank a public candidate universe, only privately authenticated and consenting nominees enter the tally, and the sole public output is the winner — with no leakage of the hidden nomination set beyond what the winner itself implies, and no exposure of individual nominees' choices through their communications.
why: It would enable leadership recruitment in settings where standing, declining, or losing invites retaliation, so any visible sign of nomination or refusal is dangerous.

title: Silent-Exit Delegation — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election protocol let voters delegate, revoke, or override their ballots privately, so that nothing beyond the winning outcome is ever revealed? The question is whether this is achievable under fixed cycle semantics and delegation-cap rules while withstanding malicious participants.
status: No protocol is known; the main obstacles identified are that cycle semantics, recovery, update races, and graph-scale costs lack precise treatment, and that device control can defeat private revocation. Anonymous credentials and malicious-secure MPC are the suggested building blocks.
solved_when: A protocol exists that supports private delegation, revocation, and ballot overriding within the fixed cycle and delegation-cap constraints, publishes only the winner, and gives precise treatment of cycle semantics, recovery, and update races with graph-scale costs bounded and private revocation secure even against device control.
why: It would enable representative decision-making without producing a public map of loyalty and withdrawal — who delegates to whom, and who pulls out, stays private.

title: Unreportable Ballot — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Can an election scheme be designed in which voters, under private-registration and safe-voting assumptions, can defeat coercion — for example by presenting a decoy credential or overriding a coerced submission — while the decisive ballots remain publicly unclassified? The goal is a construction that reveals only the authorized outcome and no more.
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known beyond the starting point of Civitas's credential-based coercion resistance. An unobserved registration or voting opportunity remains essential — cryptography cannot manufacture privacy under continuous physical or client surveillance.
solved_when: A concrete protocol exists in which, given private registration and a safe (unobserved) voting opportunity, a coerced voter can deploy a decoy credential or override a coerced submission, and the public election record does not distinguish which ballots were decisive.
why: It delivers winner-only elections with a carefully specified avenue for resisting coercion, letting voters resist coercion without the public learning anything beyond the outcome.

title: Split-Voice Testimony Channel — proposal
open: Can we build a testimony channel in which the act of receiving authorized testimony grants the recipient neither the ability to contact the speaker again nor any power to identify them, with each sender–recipient relationship governed by its own independent policy?
status: Open problems include adaptive corruption and cross-policy linkage, which require composition proofs; stylometry, disclosed facts, or a compromised endpoint can identify the speaker. Related systems include Dissent and Vuvuzela.
solved_when: A construction exists for which each relationship enforces a separate policy, and composition proofs show that adaptive corruption and cross-policy linkage attacks cannot identify or re-contact a speaker.
why: It would let witnesses contribute evidence without surrendering permanent contactability or identification capabilities to the recipient.

title: Contradiction-Preserving Testimony Bundles — proposal
open: Can an event bundle be released so that every admitted, consented claim is included, with a proof that no formal contradiction — whether favorable or unfavorable to any party — was selectively suppressed? A sharpened version asks for a testimony mixnet construction that certifies both inclusion and formal contradiction classification for the full bundle.
status: Event matching can be wrong, and semantic contradiction requires judgment; the proof certifies inclusion and formal classification, never truth. Related infrastructure comes from publicly auditable MPC and Dissent.
solved_when: A released bundle carries a publicly verifiable proof that all admitted, consented claims are present and that the formal-contradiction classification of each is preserved without selective suppression.
why: It lets inquiries preserve genuine uncertainty instead of manufacturing consensus, giving auditors a tamper-evident record of what was actually testified — including what contradicts what.

title: Amendment Without Exposure — proposal
open: Can a mixnet-based testimony system allow a witness to amend permitted fields of an already-submitted statement before a cutoff, so that recipients always see the authorized current version yet learn nothing about who edited it, when, or how often? Formally, this asks for concealed revision linkage with auditable release semantics layered onto an anonymous-submission channel.
status: The Shield system already supports modification of submitted testimony; the proposed addition is concealed revision linkage with auditable release semantics, with published copies remaining intact. Related infrastructure includes Shield and Riposte.
solved_when: A construction exists in which, prior to a stated cutoff, a witness may replace permitted fields of a record; recipients retrieve only the authorized current version; and the system reveals no information about the editor's identity, the timing, or the frequency of edits, while previously published copies remain intact and release semantics stay auditable.
why: Without it, every correction becomes a fresh metadata trail — who fixed what and when — that can be exploited as a targeting signal against the witness; with it, honest corrections carry no such exposure.

title: Patient Cross-Examination Relay — proposal
open: Can a relay of mixnet servers let questioners conduct multi-round cross-examination of witnesses over metadata-hiding channels, where endpoints exchange fixed-rate padded traffic and each questioner receives an answer—or an indication that none was ready—only at fixed epochs? The goal is a construction in which timing and message counts reveal nothing beyond the fixed schedule.
status: Existing systems such as Vuvuzela and Riposte hide transport activity, but not answer semantics from the questioner. Delays, outages, and adaptive questioning still need a composable leakage model.
solved_when: A mixnet construction exists in which all endpoints send and receive at a fixed padded rate, answers (or explicit "no answer ready" signals) are delivered only at fixed epochs, and this holds under a composable leakage model covering delays, outages, and adaptive questioning.
why: It would let follow-up scrutiny of a witness proceed interactively without the transport layer broadcasting the witness's daily schedule or answer activity.

title: Content-Blind Disruption Tribunal — proposal
open: Can a testimony mixnet revoke a submission credential only on the basis of a proved protocol violation — such as malformed traffic or unauthorized duplicate writes — without any authority ever inspecting or judging the content of what was submitted? More formally, is there a disruption tribunal that is content-blind yet sufficient to control abuse?
status: Omission and network failure are currently known to require explicit synchrony assumptions; silence alone cannot establish culpability. Related ideas include Dissent's accountability and formal protocol accountability.
solved_when: A mixnet design exists in which credential revocation occurs only upon a demonstrable protocol violation (e.g., malformed traffic or unauthorized duplicate writes), with no content-based or discretionary censorship capability, and where omission and network failure are handled under explicit synchrony assumptions rather than inferred from silence.
why: It would give testimony infrastructure disruption control without handing any operator a discretionary content-censorship switch; conversely, without it, controlling abuse seems to require either content inspection or blaming parties for silence they may not be responsible for.

title: Cohort-Bound Release Mixnet — proposal
open: Can a mixnet release a statement only when its batch satisfies contributor-chosen thresholds on cohort size and credential composition, retaining it sealed otherwise? Formally, construct a release mechanism whose publication condition is exactly the predicate chosen by the contributing witnesses, with no leakage from the failure/holding path.
status: Cohort size alone is not an anonymity theorem — adversarial contributors and recognizable content can collapse protection, and failure behavior also leaks. Prior art includes secure allegation escrows and accountable anonymous groups, but the proposed cohort-bound release mechanism remains an open construction target.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that (i) publishes a statement only in a batch meeting the contributor-specified count and credential-composition conditions, (ii) keeps it sealed (and leaks nothing, including about failure behavior) when the conditions are unmet.
why: Small communities gain a publication rule that cannot isolate a surviving witness: no statement goes out unless enough appropriately credentialed peers released alongside it.
key_works: Secure allegation escrows; accountable anonymous groups.

title: Source-Independent Testimony Lottery — proposal
open: Can a testimony mixnet admit accounts into a lottery so that, once the lottery's distribution is fixed, admission depends on no source identity and no source content — except for explicitly declared strata? The formal goal is a construction in which no participant, and no coalition, can bias which admitted accounts are drawn, nor abort an unfavorable outcome.
status: Currently, admission can be biased and unfavorable draws aborted; even with redraws prohibited, correct sampling is not necessarily unbiased conditional on completion. Related limits come from Cleve's coin-flipping impossibility results and the Dissent system.
solved_when: A protocol exists for sampling admitted accounts under a frozen distribution that is independent of source identity and content (apart from declared strata), prohibits redraws, and achieves this even though correct sampling need not be unbiased conditional on completion.
why: It would let an overwhelmed public inquiry allocate attention fairly without any single institution being able to curate the record by biasing admission or killing unfavorable draws.

title: Unlinkable Omission Challenge — proposal
open: Can a depositor prove that a ciphertext the system acknowledged as received and eligible was nevertheless left out of the committed set of inputs that were actually processed? A sharper version asks for such an omission proof that is unlinkable — revealing nothing that ties the challenge back to the depositor.
status: The known failure mode is that transferable receipts can become coercion evidence. One proposed mitigation combines designated-verifier intake handling with aggregate omission verdicts; collaborative proof generation by itself has not been shown to provide nontransferability. Related lines include publicly auditable MPC and Dissent.
solved_when: A deposit protocol exists in which a depositor can, from an acknowledgment of an eligible ciphertext, produce a proof that the ciphertext is absent from the published commitment to the processing set, and the proof is nontransferable (designated-verifier or otherwise unusable as coercion evidence against the depositor).
why: It lets witnesses challenge the quiet suppression of inconvenient evidence; without nontransferability, the very receipts needed to challenge can be turned into coercion evidence against the challenger.

title: Treaty Circuit Court — proposal
open: Can a set of parties that have already agreed on a deterministic rule — a deadline, an arithmetic obligation, or some other predicate over committed facts — obtain a verifiable evaluation of that rule on authenticated inputs without installing any external arbiter, such that acknowledged dispute flags or missing attestations yield a well-defined out-of-scope verdict rather than an ambiguous failure?
status: This is a proposal with no known construction. As stated, the circuit cannot discover unreported factual disputes, interpret unrestricted law, or compel physical enforcement. Related lines of work include SPDZ and publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A protocol exists that evaluates any agreed deterministic predicate over authenticated committed inputs, returns a defined outside-scope result on acknowledged dispute flags or missing attestations, and requires no recognized arbitrator or external court.
why: It would let encoded deadlines, arithmetic obligations, and other agreed predicates settle automatically, without any party having to recognize another institution's court.

title: Ambiguity-Envelope Court — proposal
open: Can a set of parties who disagree on how a rule should be interpreted nevertheless reach an auditable, binding disposition without any arbitrator? The proposal is to fix a finite family of plausible interpretations in advance and output a result only when every interpretation in the family yields the same authorized outcome.
status: Currently a proposal only. Known limitations: the interpretation family must be fixed in advance and cannot capture arbitrary meanings; large families are expensive; and ambiguity itself leaks information. Related tooling: publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A protocol exists that commits to a finite interpretation family fixed beforehand, and issues a disposition exactly when all interpretations in the family produce the same authorized result — using publicly auditable MPC and no trusted arbitrator.
why: It would let automated systems establish common ground and act legitimately even where constitutional, historical, or theological disagreements prevent agreeing on a single authoritative meaning.

title: Minimal-Counterexample Appeal — proposal
open: Can a party appeal a committed claim by proving that just one of its premises or computation steps admits a counterexample, while releasing nothing beyond the identifier of the invalidated clause?
status: Clause identity can itself expose a sensitive fact, so admissibility and credibility need agreed rules; "minimal" does not automatically mean private. Related lines of work include public MPC auditing and protocol accountability.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which an appeal demonstrates an admissible counterexample to exactly one committed premise or computation step, and the only information disclosed is the invalidated clause identifier.
why: It enables narrow correction of demonstrable errors without transferring an opponent's evidence.

title: Hidden-Remedy Pareto Court — proposal
open: Can a set of parties jointly compute a restitution remedy that is provably Pareto efficient with respect to their (hidden, possibly strategic) submitted utilities, without any trusted arbitrator? Formally: produce a feasible remedy together with a proof that no permitted alternative weakly improves every submitted utility while strictly improving at least one.
status: This is a proposal; no protocol or result exists yet. The key open caveat is that submitted preferences can be strategic, so Pareto efficiency for those preferences establishes neither justice nor proportionality. Key works: SPDZ; publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A protocol outputs a feasible remedy and a verifiable proof of Pareto efficiency over the submitted utility functions — no permitted alternative weakly improves every submitted utility while strictly improving at least one — under strategic submission of preferences and without a trusted arbitrator.
why: It uncovers restitution forms that public positional bargaining might never discover, replacing adversarial negotiation with verifiable computation.

title: Venue-Before-Facts Router — proposal
open: Can a party with a sensitive dispute determine which of several committed arbitration procedures actually has jurisdiction over it, without disclosing the dispute to any authority that turns out to lack jurisdiction? Formally, hidden jurisdictional attributes must select either one committed procedure or the outcome "no agreed venue," and rejected venues must receive no case.
status: This is a proposal with no known construction. Known obstacles: revealing a unique destination can reveal facts, and routing rules can discriminate; cryptography cannot create legitimate jurisdiction. Related technical tools are those of SPDZ and metadata-private messaging.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the only outputs are the single selected venue (or "no agreed venue"), no rejected venue learns anything about the case, and the unique destination is revealed without enabling the routing rules to discriminate among disputants.
why: It would allow redress without first disclosing a sensitive dispute to every rival authority — pursuing justice without exposing oneself to the authorities one is ultimately not litigating before.

title: Fact-Sensitivity Certificate — proposal
open: Can a committed arbitration procedure certify, for a declared admissible range of factual inputs, either that its outcome is invariant across that entire range or that two admissible input assignments would yield different dispositions?
status: Universal checks may be intractable, and admissible ranges may encode bias; moreover, the sensitivity result itself leaks information. The proposed approach composes publicly auditable MPC with checked solver certificates.
solved_when: A procedure exists that, for any committed admissible input range, outputs either a certificate of outcome invariance or exhibits two admissible assignments producing different dispositions, under the composition of publicly auditable MPC with checked solver certificates.
why: It would give formal arbitration that can identify exactly when human fact-finding is necessary, distinguishing cases resolvable mechanically from those that turn on contested facts.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC, composed with checked solver certificates.

title: Sealed-Precedent Consistency Gate — proposal
open: Can a sealed proceeding yield an enforceable consistency guarantee — that equivalent cases under an agreed feature relation receive consistent dispositions or an authorized, scoped exception — without any arbitrator seeing the case contents?
status: The equivalence relation is normative. Missing or selectively committed precedents remain an input-governance problem; related approaches draw on publicly auditable MPC and protocol accountability.
solved_when: A mechanism exists under which any pair of cases equivalent under the agreed feature relation provably receives either identical dispositions or an exception explicitly authorized and scoped by the system's rules.
why: It would let confidential settlements support procedural consistency instead of enabling secret double standards, reconciling privacy with equal treatment under precedent.

title: Appeal-Latched Escrow Judgment — proposal
open: Can an escrowed judgment be designed so that funds are released only once a valid disposition exists and every acknowledged timely appeal has been resolved, with no trusted arbitrator?
status: Currently a proposal. Filing censorship is not handled by the scheme and needs its own challenge mechanism; availability, escrow enforcement, and abort recovery remain additional assumptions. Related lines of work include zero-knowledge contingent payments and fairness limits.
solved_when: A mechanism is specified in which escrow release is provably gated on (i) a valid disposition and (ii) resolution of every acknowledged timely appeal, and this gating holds under the stated assumptions.
why: It prevents a party from using the system to execute an award while suppressing an acknowledged appeal, giving escrow-backed arbitration real enforcement power.

title: Survivor Branch Certificate — proposal
open: Can a claimant prove, in a verifiable way, that they hold an attested path to a qualifying historical-event credential under a published kinship policy? More precisely, the problem is to design a certificate mechanism that lets such a path be demonstrated without requiring the underlying attestations to establish anything beyond recorded relationships.
status: Attestations establish recorded relationships, including recognized adoption — not historical truth or moral worth. Destroyed records and dishonest issuers remain unresolved obstacles. Related technical foundations include Coconut and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a claimant can prove an attested path to a qualifying credential under a published kinship policy, where attestations are understood to establish recorded relationships (including recognized adoption) but not historical truth or moral worth.
why: It would enable scholarships or memorial access to be administered through identifiable survivor-family registers, which are currently absent.

title: Equal-Kin Edge — proposal
open: Can a party prove that a family tie belongs to an authorized equivalence class of qualifying kinship relations without revealing which specific mechanism — adoption, guardianship, or biological descent — produced that tie? Formalized, this asks for a proof system that certifies membership in the permitted kinship class while the underlying edge type remains hidden.
status: No scheme is known; this is a proposal. Current practice treats agreement about qualifying relations as a governance matter, and unequal documentation requirements can exclude otherwise eligible applicants; moreover, even successful eligibility checks can imply background information about the applicant. Candidate tools are anonymous credentials and signatures of knowledge, but the problem remains open.
solved_when: A proof or credential scheme exists that (i) accepts exactly the kinship edges in the permitted equivalence class, and (ii) reveals nothing about whether a given qualifying edge arose from adoption, guardianship, or biological descent.
why: It lets benefits and entitlements honor all recognized family forms while protecting applicants from disclosure of adoption or guardianship status — disclosures that unequally documented applicants might otherwise be forced to make, and that can leak background information beyond eligibility itself.

title: Ash-Witness Enrollment — proposal
open: Can a family relationship that has been hidden or destroyed be attested by multiple distinct authorized witnesses drawn from different institutions, such that their combined testimony authorizes the claim without any single witness revealing what they know?
status: Currently a proposal, with no construction known; foundational tools are the Coconut signature scheme and zero-knowledge sets.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which only authorized, institutionally diverse witnesses can jointly attest a hidden relationship claim, quorum failure reveals nothing about the claim's truth, and institutional diversity alone is never taken as proof of independent memory or truthfulness.
why: It would restore access for families whose documents disappeared through displacement or deliberate destruction, where no single institution's records survive or can be trusted alone.

title: Family Entitlement Algebra — proposal
open: Can a committed family benefit be split into shares that individual claimants control and keep private, while the total still obeys an authorized succession rule — even when not all potential relatives are known in advance?
status: Conservation of the benefit is currently defined only over the enrolled roster, leaving unknown relatives outside its guarantee; contested enrollment and corrections still lack explicit rules for freezing or revising allocations. Relevant techniques appear in provisions' confidential accounting and anonymous credentials.
solved_when: A construction exists in which shares are hidden from all parties except their claimant, the sum of shares respects the authorized succession rule, and explicit rules govern freezing or revising allocations when enrollment is contested or corrected.
why: It would let compensation pass to estranged and dispersed family members without exposing who claims what, and without a contested enrollment silently invalidating the allocation.

title: Unlinkable Claim Constellation — proposal
open: Can multiple benefit programs jointly disburse survivor-related payments so that no program learns more than whether its proposed payment fits a shared cap, with the claimant alone receiving the remaining balance — and no party able to link claimants across programs? A construction achieving this, with an explicit threat model, is the target.
status: This is a proposal only. Known weaknesses: timing patterns and unusual amounts can identify people, and enrollment, recovery, and atomic balance updates still require explicit threat models. Related primitives exist in the literature on anonymous credentials and Provisions.
solved_when: A concrete protocol exists in which each program learns only whether its proposed payment fits the joint cap, the claimant receives the remaining balance, enrollment/recovery/atomic balance updates are handled, and timing- and amount-based identification channels are addressed under a stated threat model.
why: It would let survivors carry portable support across countries and institutions without enabling routine cross-program tracking of who they are or what they receive.

title: Lineage Repair Cascade — proposal
open: When a genealogical record is corrected by a signed statement, can the correction invalidate only the eligibility decisions that depended on the erroneous lineage, while allowing repaired or unaffected descent paths to re-establish their standing privately — without exposing the correction's ripple effects to outsiders?
status: Efficient private refresh across enormous dependency graphs remains an open integration target; relevant building blocks are dynamic accumulators and proof-carrying data. Past disclosure cannot be undone, and clawbacks require policy rather than purely cryptographic treatment.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a signed invalidation propagates through the dependency graph so that stale downstream eligibilities become unverifiable, yet holders on repaired or unaffected paths can refresh their credentials privately; the mechanism must scale to enormous dependency graphs.
why: It prevents an archival mistake from becoming public stigma: individuals affected by a correction lose eligibility without their genealogical circumstances being broadcast.

title: Veiled Eligibility Union — proposal
open: Can a person prove eligibility for a union of multiple authorized routes—descent, recognized kinship, or sponsorship—while disclosing nothing about which route applies?
status: Currently only a proposal; no construction is known. The requirements it must meet are that alternative routes be genuine and treated identically, since distinct timing, expiry, recovery, or outside knowledge can expose which route was used. Related groundwork includes Coconut's private attributes and anonymous credentials.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which any of the authorized routes grants admission, all routes receive equivalent treatment (no distinguishable timing, expiry, recovery, or outside-knowledge requirements), and an outside observer learns only that some route qualifies.
why: It would let survivor families receive assistance without labeling every recipient as a survivor, protecting them from the stigma or targeting that the label itself invites.

title: Mutual Kinship Beacon — proposal
open: Can a group of participants learn whether their authenticated ancestor sets intersect within an agreed generation range, without revealing anything else about their lineages? Any step toward contact disclosure must remain gated behind separate consent.
status: Currently a match reveals a relationship, which is more than intended. Repeated guesses are not bounded without authorization limits, documentary errors remain unhandled, and abort must never be allowed to force identity disclosure. Related primitives are private set intersection and threshold credentials.
solved_when: A protocol exists that outputs a kinship match exactly when the authenticated ancestor sets intersect within the agreed generation range, enforces authorization limits on repeated guesses, tolerates documentary errors, and guarantees that aborting never forces identity disclosure; all beyond the match itself requires separate consent.
why: It would let separated survivors and chosen kin reconnect without ever building a public map of survivor lineages, which could expose vulnerable people.

title: Jamarat Counterflow Covenant — proposal
open: Can a group of pilgrimage institutions, each holding private information about its members' party sizes, acceptable crossing windows, and consented (or independently justified) separation constraints, jointly compute private crossing tickets for the Jamarat ritual together with a public proof that all safety and consent rules were honored?
status: The proposal is at the concept stage. Open obstacles: the integer optimization must scale, modelled safety depends on realistic crowd bounds and compliance, and offline signatures alone cannot prevent copied-ticket redemption. Key works referenced: private coalition scheduling; collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists that takes the private inputs and outputs, for each group, tickets assigning members to crossing windows satisfying all separation constraints, plus a publicly verifiable compliance proof; the underlying integer optimization must scale to the stated crowd bounds, and ticket issuance must resist copied-ticket redemption rather than relying on offline signatures alone.
why: It enables joint movement planning among rival pilgrimage institutions that do not trust each other with their private coordination data, while still giving authorities and the public verifiable assurance of compliance.

title: Arafat Sunset Release Envelope — proposal
open: Can we compute dispatch windows for each pilgrimage operator that remain feasible for every possible arrival profile within the committed uncertainty intervals, while releasing to each operator only its own instructions? Formally, this asks for a private robust-optimization procedure whose per-operator outputs are jointly feasible across the whole uncertainty set without any party holding all schedules.
status: Private robust optimization is understood to need support for safe rolling updates, since an operator’s own released instructions can imply delays for another group; behavior outside the model remains outside the guarantee. Related work includes Otti and private coalition scheduling.
solved_when: A method exists that, given the committed uncertainty intervals over arrival profiles, produces dispatch windows guaranteed feasible for every profile in those intervals, and each operator learns nothing beyond its own instructions.
why: It enables delay-tolerant departure planning without any central authority possessing all operators' schedules, which is what currently blocks confidential coalition coordination.

title: Mina Three-Way Exchange — proposal
open: Can a group of pilgrims find a mutually acceptable three-way exchange of capacity or accommodation, where each participant privately proves consent and that resources are conserved, without revealing their bargaining positions? Formally, construct a protocol that identifies a consented exchange cycle while keeping individual preferences and acceptance decisions confidential.
status: This is currently a proposal. Repeated hypothetical swaps are known to reveal preferences. Atomicity concerns the reservation ledger — providers must honor it, and MPC cannot compel simultaneous physical execution. Related approaches draw on secure stable matching and optimization proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists that finds a consented cycle of capacity or accommodation exchanges, privately proving each party's acceptance and the conservation of resources, without repeated swaps or direct bilateral negotiation.
why: It enables itinerary adjustments among pilgrims without broadcasting bargaining positions or requiring direct pairwise negotiation, which repeated hypothetical swaps would otherwise expose.

title: Muzdalifah Exception Cloak — proposal
open: Can a pilgrim be granted an alternative movement window after proving they qualify for an exception, without revealing their diagnosis or which credential branch entitled them to it?
status: The assigned service can itself identify the exception, which limits the achievable privacy; credential policy and service design must address this, and visible accommodations remain visible. Related approaches draw on Coconut and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which an authorized pilgrim proves an accepted exception predicate and receives an alternative movement window, with both the diagnosis and the qualifying credential branch hidden from the coordination system; the same privacy guarantees must hold even though the assigned service can itself identify the exception, and visible accommodations remain visible.
why: It enables private accommodation of health, disability, or other authorized needs, so pilgrims are not forced to expose sensitive medical or credential information to receive entitled services.

title: Rite-Order Private Witness — proposal
open: Can a pilgrim prove in zero knowledge that their private itinerary complies with one authorized rule system drawn from an agreed family, and satisfies all shared capacity constraints, without revealing which rule branch they follow?
status: A proposal exists, but communities must still validate their rule encodings; formal compatibility does not establish religious validity. Related directions include zero-knowledge planning and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A zero-knowledge proof system (e.g., zk-SNARK-based) exists in which a prover demonstrates both (i) compliance with some rule system in the agreed family and (ii) satisfaction of all shared capacity constraints, while the selected rule branch remains hidden from verifiers and collaborators.
why: It enables coordination across accepted ritual interpretations without exposing personal adherence, allowing heterogeneous communities to share logistics and capacity without religious disclosure.

title: Crowd Slack Without Counts — proposal
open: Can a pilgrimage coordinator publish a conservative band of additional admissions — a range rather than an exact count — and prove that doing so never erodes the capacity reserves already committed to pilgrims?
status: Exact repeated slack answers can reconstruct demand, so the leakage account must include denials, rounding, and physical observations; related work appears in private scheduling and privacy filters.
solved_when: A released additional-admission band is accompanied by a proof that committed capacity reserves are preserved, and the leakage account covers denials, rounding, and physical observations.
why: It lets gate staff make useful admission decisions without handing a central authority exact, reconstructable demand information.

title: Limited-Disruption Rerouting — proposal
open: After a route closure is authenticated, can the coordinator issue revised private tickets and certify that at most a specified number of tickets changed, while the agreed privacy protections remain intact?
status: A bounded repair may not exist. Failure needs an explicit result and a pre-agreed physical fallback.
solved_when: A protocol exists that, given an authenticated closure, produces revised tickets together with a certificate that no more than the specified bound of tickets changed, without disclosing complete itineraries; alternatively, an explicit result showing no such bounded repair exists, paired with a pre-agreed physical fallback procedure.
why: It enables auditable rerouting of pilgrims after disruptions without revealing anyone's complete itinerary, so coordination can be verified publicly while travel plans stay private.

title: Hajj Ticket Epoch Lock — proposal
open: How can a replacement pilgrimage schedule be made to take effect safely, activating only after a guard interval that covers clock skew and the clearance of all previously authorized movements? The question is to design an epoch-lock mechanism so that split views, delayed updates, and fallback activations can never produce overlapping occupancy of the same allocation slot.
status: This is a proposal. Current considerations note that split views, delayed updates, and fallback activation must not create overlapping occupancy, and that secret sharing supplies neither consensus nor a trustworthy physical clock. Key works: Coconut; universally composable protocol analysis.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which no replacement schedule becomes active before a guard interval sufficient for clock skew and for previously authorized movements to clear has elapsed, and in which concurrent or fallback activations provably cannot yield overlapping occupancy.
why: It enables private allocation changes despite intermittent connectivity and hostile operators, which secret sharing alone cannot deliver since it supplies neither consensus nor a trustworthy physical clock.

title: Equal-Precedence Rotation — proposal
open: Can passage windows at a crossing with no institutional primacy be allocated so that each party's cumulative delay stays privately accounted while the rotation rule itself is publicly chosen? In other words, is there a protocol that couples private cumulative-delay balances with an agreed public rotation to schedule crossings fairly?
status: Comparable burdens and authenticated delays are known to require agreement and measurement, and the rotation rule's fairness is currently a premise rather than a cryptographic conclusion.
solved_when: A protocol exists that allocates passage windows under a publicly chosen rotation rule while maintaining private cumulative-delay balances for each party, such that no repeated arrangement can silently convert temporary priority into permanent precedence.
why: It prevents repeated crossing arrangements from entrenching temporary priority as permanent precedence, which is what breaks when fairness is only assumed rather than enforced.

title: Multi-Calendar Collision Oracle — proposal
open: Can private parties holding sensitive event intervals discover, without revealing which institutions participate or which routes are involved, only the coarse time periods in which coordination would be required? In formal terms: is there a multi-calendar collision oracle that outputs nothing beyond these coarse periods?
status: No protocol currently achieves this; the record is a proposal. Known obstacles are that a rare observance may be identifiable from a conflict flag, and that repeated forecasts and uncertain dates require explicit leakage analysis. Related primitives include PICS committed-set intersection and private scheduling.
solved_when: A protocol exists that, given private event intervals from multiple institutions with independent date-setting procedures, outputs the coarse coordination periods while withholding participant identities and routes — accompanied by an explicit leakage analysis covering the risk that a rare observance is identifiable from a conflict flag and the setting of repeated forecasts with uncertain dates.
why: It enables early coordination while each institution retains control of its own calendar and date-setting procedures, so scheduling across institutions does not force anyone to expose their observances or internal planning.

title: Doorway Lease Without Title — proposal
open: Can a cryptographic credential be constructed that authorizes exactly one specified action at an agreed doorway during one agreed interval, while proving the required custodial approvals — and nothing more?
status: This is a proposal; the constraint is that the credential's institutional meaning must stay narrow, with physical enforcement and key governance treated as external to the credential itself. Candidate building blocks are Coconut credentials and general-access-structure MPC.
solved_when: A credential exists that (i) permits only the single specified action, (ii) is valid only during the single agreed interval, (iii) carries proof of the required custodial approvals, and (iv) creates no legitimate title or broader institutional claim beyond the narrow agreement.
why: It would let parties enter small, reversible agreements — such as temporary passage rights — even while larger ownership or authority claims remain unresolved, without conceding anything in that larger dispute.

title: Headway Under Secret Delays — proposal
open: Can two parties each holding a private committed schedule jointly determine, without revealing those schedules, whether every possible timing realization within their mutually accepted uncertainty sets still preserves the agreed headway constraints at shared crossings?
status: No protocol is known. The core obstacles identified are that declared timing bounds must be credible, that repeated narrowing of the uncertainty sets can leak the underlying schedule, and that mathematical separation between plans does not by itself control actual physical movement. Related directions include private scheduling and zero-knowledge planning.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which both groups learn only whether headway is preserved for every timing realization in the accepted uncertainty sets, while neither group's routes or full timetable is disclosed.
why: It enables local crossing verification — groups can confirm safe separation without surrendering proprietary routes or complete timetables to any central authority or to each other.

title: Acoustic Truce Budget — proposal
open: Can several institutions sharing an acoustic space each privately specify the sound intervals and levels they find acceptable, and jointly learn which uses are permitted, without any institution revealing more than the resulting agreement? Formally, this asks for a jointly specified acoustic model in which acceptable sound intervals and levels are allocated privately, with each institution's permissions revealed only as the output.
status: Open as a proposal. The acoustic model, the measurement locations, and the acceptable burdens still need to be agreed upon. Audible events remain observable regardless of transcript privacy. Related work includes Otti's numerical verification and work on private scheduling.
solved_when: The parties reach agreement on the acoustic model, the measurement locations, and the acceptable burdens, and a private allocation mechanism outputs each institution's permitted sound intervals and levels without disclosing individual inputs beyond that output.
why: It enables specific soundscape agreements without requiring institutions to publish their future observance plans, so commitments can be reached while observance remains unannounced.

title: Affiliation-Blind Passage — proposal
open: Can a traveler prove they hold a valid reservation and satisfy eligibility under an authorized rule, without revealing which issuing branch granted it or what destinations lie beyond the current checkpoint?
status: Open proposal. Known obstacles are side channels — clothing, companions, routes, and timing can expose affiliation — and small eligibility classes and issuer metadata must be addressed. Key works: Coconut; Path ORAM.
solved_when: A proof system exists that validates reservation and rule-based eligibility while hiding issuer branch and downstream destinations, and that moreover resists the known leakage channels: affiliation revealed through clothing, companions, routes, or timing, and membership in small eligibility classes or issuer metadata.
why: It would let shared access systems operate without building religious-affiliation registers, protecting travelers from institutional profiling.

title: Counterfactual Delay Appeal — proposal
open: Can a system certify, for a rejected appellant, that some feasible alternative schedule would have improved the appellant's burden by an agreed threshold, without degrading others' protected conditions? In formal terms: produce a proof of the existence (or non-existence) of such a feasible alternative, efficient enough to run within a fixed appeal budget.
status: As a proposal, no solution exists yet. The known obstacles are that repeated threshold appeals effectively become a preference oracle, and that large combinatorial instances require efficient proofs under a fixed appeal budget. Related work includes Otti and privacy filters.
solved_when: There is a procedure that, on each appeal, either certifies a feasible alternative improving the appellant's burden by the agreed threshold while preserving others' protected conditions, or certifies that none exists — and does so with efficient proofs even for large combinatorial instances, within a fixed appeal budget.
why: It grounds scheduling appeals in verifiable alternatives rather than compelled calendar disclosure, and keeps repeated threshold appeals from degenerating into a preference oracle that leaks others' private scheduling data.

title: Sanctuary Escape Reserve — proposal
open: Can every confidential resource allocation be guaranteed to keep an agreed escape reserve intact across a bounded family of emergency scenarios? Formally, the allocation must remain consistent with a reserve requirement holding under each scenario in the family.
status: A conservative physical model has been proposed but needs validation; arithmetic alone cannot certify outcomes under unmodeled crowds, obstructed infrastructure, or emergency-time compliance.
solved_when: A confidential allocation scheme exists that provably preserves the agreed escape reserve across the entire bounded family of emergency scenarios, with validation covering unmodeled crowds, obstructed infrastructure, and compliance behavior during an emergency.
why: It would enable private everyday scheduling of a shared space while maintaining an auditable emergency-access floor — confidential use does not come at the cost of guaranteed escape capacity.

title: Reciprocal Gesture Seal — proposal
open: Can messages be sealed at commitment time so that none becomes readable until every required matching authorization has been collected, while an audit ledger alone does not suffice?
status: A ledger by itself is only an audit log and does not yield fair release; fairness requires specified escrow, availability, timing, and corruption assumptions, and earlier abort remains possible. Related literature includes zero-knowledge contingent exchange and fairness limits.
solved_when: A release mechanism exists under explicitly specified escrow, availability, timing, and corruption assumptions, in which precommitted messages are releasable only once all required matching authorizations exist; abort prior to full authorization remains permitted.
why: It would enable reciprocal acknowledgments or invitations without either party risking unilateral prepublication exposure.

title: Graduated Reciprocity Ratchet — proposal
open: Can post-war reconciliation commitments be structured as a graduated ratchet, in which each side must satisfy the currently authenticated conditions before the protocol advances, while unused future concessions remain withheld? In other words, is there a committed state machine design that accumulates verifiable mutual progress without requiring total initial disclosure from either party?
status: Open obstacles: attestations do not prove physical performance; abort can signal readiness rather than defection; and rigid stages can conflict with changing consent. Key works: SPDZ; formal accountability.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which a committed state machine advances only when each side satisfies the current authenticated conditions, with unused future concessions withheld until their stage is reached.
why: It would enable reconciliation that accumulates verifiable progress step by step, rather than demanding total initial disclosure before any trust is established.

title: Noncanceling Responsibility Ledger — proposal
open: Can we design a ledger of post-war responsibility obligations in which opposing obligations never cancel automatically, so that each obligation — carrying its own private beneficiary scope and remedy type — can only be discharged with the explicit conversion authorization of its required beneficiaries?
status: Types and releases still need agreement among the parties; cryptography cannot establish moral equivalence, factual performance, or control of off-system settlements. Relevant tools include provisions and publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A ledger design exists in which obligations carry private beneficiary scopes and remedy types, and cancellation or conversion of opposing obligations is impossible without explicit authorization from the required beneficiaries; the remaining coordination tasks (types and releases requiring agreement) are characterized precisely.
why: It would allow mutual acknowledgment between conflicting parties without imposing an automatic arithmetic equivalence between different kinds of harms, which current mechanisms cannot respect.

title: Acknowledgment Without Endorsement — proposal
open: Can we design a receipt that certifies only that an exact statement was received and a named mechanical check was completed, while conveying no agreement, understanding, or admission — and can it be made robust to outsourcing and misrepresentation by public actors?
status: This is a proposal. Digital checks cannot establish attention or comprehension and can be outsourced; public actors may still misrepresent the receipt. Related ideas appear in designated-verifier proofs and protocol accountability.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the receipt provably establishes possession of the exact statement and completion of the specified check, and nothing more; and in which neither outsourcing of the check nor a public actor's misrepresentation yields an endorsement-equivalent claim.
why: It gives evidence that grievances reached authorized channels without forcing the aggrieved party to endorse anything — a building block for post-war reconciliation commitments where acknowledgment must not imply consent.

title: Forgiveness Capability Firewall — proposal
open: Can a person’s credential for participating in reconciliation be constructed so that it authorizes only the specific interactions it names, and is cryptographically or architecturally incapable of satisfying software checks for unrelated settlement, testimony release, or waiver? In short: is a capability firewall around "forgiveness" tokens achievable?
status: This is a proposal. The envisioned mechanism is type separation governing software checks, but it does not govern legal interpretation or social pressure, and other people can still mischaracterize participation. Related ideas include designated-verifier proofs and Shield’s mutable consent-related records.
solved_when: A credential design exists in which a token issued for specified reconciliation interactions provably cannot be accepted by any software check governing unrelated settlement, testimony release, or waiver.
why: It would let people take part in reconciliation processes without a platform-level surrender of unrelated rights.
key_works: Designated-verifier proofs; Shield’s mutable consent-related records.

title: Safe-Continuation Discovery — proposal
open: Does there exist, for a bounded state machine, a contingent policy that preserves private limits even when disruptions, environmental moves, and withdrawal options are declared up front? If so, can such a policy be certified as safe?
status: A winning policy may not exist. Environmental moves, withdrawal rights, state-space costs, and output-trace leakage all require explicit treatment. Adjacent proof targets include publicly auditable MPC and zero-knowledge planning.
solved_when: A policy for the bounded state machine is exhibited together with a certificate that it preserves private limits under declared disruptions and withdrawal options, with environmental moves, state-space costs, and output-trace leakage explicitly handled.
why: A solution would let parties enter initial cooperation with checkable protections against later procedural traps.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; zero-knowledge planning as an adjacent proof target.

title: Non-Accusatory Incident Fuse — proposal
open: Can we design an incident mechanism in which a secret report that satisfies a pre-committed corroboration predicate triggers only a bounded pause or a verification request — with any attribution deferred to a separate, independent process?
