status: Coordinated false reports may satisfy a weak predicate, and pauses can be weaponized, so limits and a contest mechanism are considered necessary. Relevant key works include secure allegation escrows and publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which reports meeting the committed predicate provably yield a bounded pause or verification request, attribution is achievable only via the separate process, and the mechanism resists coordinated false reports while including explicit pause limits and a contest mechanism.
why: It lets fragile post-war reconciliation processes act on alarming information before accusations harden into conflict.
key_works: Secure allegation escrows; publicly auditable MPC.

title: Exit-Without-Betrayal Certificate — proposal
open: Can an exiting party certify which of its committed obligations are completed, consensually released, or still pending, without exposing the underlying negotiations or asserting moral innocence?
status: No mechanism is currently known; exit rules can become unjust as circumstances change, contested physical obligations remain unresolved, and an adversary may block certification.
solved_when: A certification mechanism exists that correctly classifies each committed obligation as completed, consensually released, or pending, while revealing nothing about negotiation contents and making no claim of moral innocence — and functions even when contested physical obligations remain unresolved or an adversary attempts to block certification.
why: It lets institutions exit a conflict or arrangement without either side being able to silently rewrite the shared process history, keeping exit rules fair as circumstances change.

title: Exculpation-Latched Disclosure — proposal
open: Can a disclosure system release every committed record matching an agreed exculpation predicate to authorized defense recipients, while the formally linked rebuttals remain protected as specified — i.e., can release be "latched" to exculpation so incriminating and exculpatory material travel together?
status: Current guarantees cover committed records and encoded relevance only; hidden evidence, witness danger, and guilt remain substantive open questions. Related lines of work include publicly auditable MPC and allegation escrows.
solved_when: A construction exists in which all committed records matching the agreed exculpation predicate are made available to authorized defense recipients with the specified protections, such that no selective disclosure can expose accusatory material while withholding formally linked rebuttals.
why: Without it, the system can selectively disclose incriminating material while withholding formally linked rebuttals, undermining the fairness the design is meant to guarantee.

title: Cross-Bloc Corroboration Option — proposal
open: Can a sealed transitional-justice process be designed so that reports independently reaching an agreed diversity-of-attestation rule generate confidential follow-up eligibility, while any further disclosure requires fresh consent from the witness?
status: Currently a proposal only; no mechanism is established. The open concern is that credential diversity is not factual independence, and that false matching, strategic enrollment, and threshold-breaking withdrawals require careful treatment. Key works: secure allegation escrows; Shield.
solved_when: A specified mechanism exists in which reports meeting an agreed diversity-of-attestation rule trigger only confidential follow-up eligibility, all further disclosure is gated on fresh consent, and the treatment of false matching, strategic enrollment, and threshold-breaking withdrawals is explicitly handled.
why: Witnesses could discover support across hostile institutions without creating a public accusation, enabling corroboration where no single institution can be trusted with the fact of contact.

title: Adversarial Due-Process Aperture — proposal
open: Can every authorized defense question be given a predetermined evidentiary view together with a completeness proof relative to the committed records — even when some accusations cannot be meaningfully challenged without identifying a source, so the protocol must instead report incompatibility whenever protection and adequate scrutiny cannot coexist?
status: Some accusations cannot be meaningfully challenged without identifying a source; the protocol must report incompatibility when protection and adequate scrutiny cannot coexist. Relevant lines of work include publicly auditable MPC and zero-knowledge selective disclosure.
solved_when: A protocol exists that, for each authorized defense question, fixes the evidentiary view in advance and produces a completeness proof against the committed records, and correctly reports incompatibility in cases where source protection and adequate scrutiny cannot coexist.
why: It would allow protected testimony to be scrutinized through demonstrably consistent views, giving sealed transitional-justice proceedings a workable form of adversarial challenge without unmasking sources.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; zero-knowledge selective disclosure.

title: Acquittal Repair Relay — proposal
open: Can an authenticated corrected disposition be relayed so that every authorized mailbox receives a linked notice, while the recipient list and any sealed evidence remain hidden from all parties, including the relay itself?
status: Currently a proposal only. The system cannot erase copies or reach undisclosed onward recipients, and availability is understood as a property of the mechanism rather than of human attention or belief. Related techniques include Vuvuzela and publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which any authorized recipient holding a prior disposition obtains the corrected, authenticated notice with a verifiable link to it, yet no party — operator, recipient, or observer — can learn the full set of recipients or the contents of sealed evidence; the system provably cannot erase existing copies or deliver to undisclosed onward recipients.
why: It enables verifiable correction propagation in transitional-justice contexts without publishing everyone connected to a case, so accountability does not come at the price of exposing protected participants.

title: Appeal Reexecution Capsule — proposal
open: Can an authorized appeal be re-executed so that the corrected rule is applied to the originally committed evidence together only with explicitly admitted amendments, with no other inputs altered or introduced?
status: This is a proposal. Correct execution cannot repair omitted evidence or legitimize a new rule; key custody, permissions, and assumptions must survive the appeal horizon. Relevant technical anchors include SPDZ and publicly auditable MPC.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which an authorized appeal provably executes the corrected rule over the original committed evidence plus explicitly admitted amendments, while key custody, permissions, and assumptions survive the appeal horizon.
why: It would allow procedural correction across political transitions without exposing witnesses to successor governments.

title: Cumulative Disclosure Firewall — proposal
open: Can we build a firewall that authorizes statistical queries only when their possible answers leave a protected attribute's uncertainty intact, even as queries accumulate? Formally, within a finite declared adversary-knowledge model, decide for each query whether its possible outputs preserve a specified level of uncertainty about protected attributes.
status: No construction is known. Universal claims are defeated by knowledge outside the declared model, and adaptive refusals together with exact inference can render the analysis difficult or intractable. Key works: Auditable MPC; metadata leakage analysis.
solved_when: A decision procedure exists that, under a finite declared adversary-knowledge model, either authorizes each query (its possible outputs preserve the specified uncertainty about protected attributes) or refuses it, so that no sequence of individually permitted queries can reduce the protected uncertainty below the specified bound.
why: It prevents individually modest questions from silently reconstructing a dossier about a protected person within the declared model — the core assurance needed for sealed transitional-justice records.

title: Necessary-Disclosure Certificate — proposal
open: Among a finite menu of views, can one be selected that meets a committed procedural sufficiency test while minimizing declared disclosure cost?
status: Sufficiency and cost are currently negotiated judgments. Cross-field inference can invalidate additive privacy costs, and richer optimization may be expensive. Related lines include publicly auditable MPC and Otti's optimization proofs.
solved_when: A view from the finite menu is identified that satisfies the committed procedural sufficiency test and achieves the minimum declared disclosure cost among the menu.
why: It lets an inquiry explain formally why a date, location, or relationship had to be revealed.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; Otti’s optimization proofs.

title: Nontransferable Issuance Receipt — proposal
open: Can a designated recipient be convinced that a sealed issuance occurred, while remaining unable to produce evidence of that issuance — or of guilt — that convinces anyone else? Formally: an issuance-receipt mechanism whose proof transcript is simulatable by the recipient, so public establishment of issuance or guilt is impossible even if the recipient repeats what they saw.
status: Recipients can repeat the information they received, and coercers can control devices, so recipient-side secrecy alone is insufficient; nontransferable evidence is a narrower goal than secrecy or protection against defamation. Key works: designated-verifier proofs; allegation escrows.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the designated recipient verifies issuance, yet the proof transcript is simulatable by that recipient; repetitions by the recipient (who can be controlled or coerced via their device) do not constitute transferable, authoritative-looking evidence of issuance or guilt.
why: It would enable private support or preliminary coordination without creating portable, authoritative-looking guilt tokens that could be used for coercion or defamation.

title: Blind Scarcity Settlement — proposal
open: Can a set of authenticated claims and a fixed budget be settled into private awards under an agreed allocation rule, without any party seeing individual claims? More precisely, can blind settlement guarantee that each award is determined by the agreed rule applied to the authenticated inputs, while no participant learns more than the aggregate allows?
status: Currently fairness of the formula and authenticity of evidence remain human responsibilities. Related techniques exist in SPDZ and Provisions, but no protocol yet addresses the twin risks that tiny aggregates and payment rails can expose recipients, or that an abort must not falsely finalize awards.
solved_when: A protocol exists that takes authenticated claims and a fixed budget, outputs private per-recipient awards matching the agreed allocation rule, and ensures that tiny aggregates and payment rails do not expose recipients and that an abort does not falsely finalize awards.
why: It enables auditable allocation of reparations and restitution without a central holder of sensitive claims, so fairness can be verified without forcing recipients to reveal what they are owed or why.

title: Hidden Deed Collision — proposal
open: Can a claimant learn that its enrolled restitution claim collides with another claim — geometrically or genealogically — without learning anything else about the rival claimant, receiving only an opaque dispute handle to carry into later resolution? Formally, this asks for a private matching protocol over uncertain historical boundaries and lineage records that outputs merely a collision bit plus handle.
status: Open problems remain on both fronts: historical boundaries need uncertainty semantics, since documents cannot decide legitimate title; and genuine-claim credentials must be designed to constrain parcel-probing attacks. Relevant techniques come from private matching and malicious MPC.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which a claimant learns only whether its claim overlaps another enrolled claim and an opaque dispute handle, with genuine-claim credentials that constrain parcel-probing attacks, and uncertainty semantics for historical boundaries built into the matching.
why: It enables early conflict handling in reparations processes without exposing families to targeted pressure or revealing which documents cannot decide legitimate title.

title: Counterfactual Compensation Envelope — proposal
open: Can a group of institutions with different assumptions about reparations jointly compute a compensation envelope — the minimum and maximum award, plus the undisputed named components — for identical claims, such that each recipient learns only the envelope and never which institution's model produced which number?
status: Model families must be frozen before outputs are computed; otherwise repeated variants of a claim can be used to reconstruct underlying claim data. Even if the models computationally agree, this establishes neither causal truth nor funding authority — the envelope bounds what a fair award could be, not what happened or who must pay it. Candidate technical tools include SPDZ and proof-carrying computation.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which (i) a fixed family of models, frozen before any outputs are produced, evaluates every claim identically, and (ii) recipients receive only the minimum award, the maximum award, and the named components that are identical across all models — with no additional leakage, including via repeated variants of the same claim.
why: It allows undisputed components of a reparations award to be paid immediately while the disputing institutions preserve their disagreement about contested assumptions, instead of blocking all payment until consensus is reached.

title: Nonwaiver Installment Receipt — proposal
open: Can a partial reparations payment be recorded in a way that provably updates the payer's outstanding balance while leaving an explicitly declared reservation of unresolved rights intact and visible?
status: It is established that a receipt itself cannot make a clause legally effective. Handling interest, inheritance, disputed deductions, and interrupted payments requires an agreed state machine; relevant techniques include provisions and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A receipt design exists in which each installment adjusts the hidden balance, the unresolved-rights reservation is preserved as policy defines it, and no clause becomes legally effective merely by being printed on a receipt.
why: Without it, early reparations payments risk being silently converted by the receiving platform into undisclosed full settlements, extinguishing claims the payee never intended to waive.

title: Reparation Reserve Curtain — proposal
open: Can a system prove, at a single accounting epoch, that its committed and unencumbered reserves are sufficient to cover all admitted hidden liabilities?
status: External encumbrances and complete liabilities currently require verification outside the circuit, and repeated solvency predicates reveal bounds; missing attestations must produce an uncertified epoch. Key works: Provisions' privacy-preserving solvency proofs.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that, at one accounting epoch, certifies reserve coverage of admitted hidden liabilities, with external encumbrances and complete liabilities verified outside the circuit, repeated solvency predicates not revealing bounds, and missing attestations yielding an uncertified epoch.
why: It would allow credible funding promises to be made without requiring public claim registers.

title: Offset Without Association — proposal
open: Can a group of restitution programs determine how much monetary compensation they may jointly award for the same underlying harm, without any of them learning which victims have also filed claims with the others? Formally, this asks for a protocol that computes permitted monetary overlap across programs covering an identical harm, while withholding all other claims and program affiliations from every party.
status: Harm equivalence is understood to require more than identity matching and to need an appeals mechanism. Known hazards are that repeated adjustments can expose earlier awards, and that poor event identifiers leak associations. Related technical tools are private set intersection and the Provisions system.
solved_when: A protocol exists that computes the permitted overlap for the same covered harm across programs, reveals no information beyond that output about other claims or affiliations, supports an appeals process for harm-equivalence determinations, and resists repeated-adjustment attacks in which successive queries expose earlier awards.
why: It would let independent reparations programs coordinate benefits without a unified victim database, which is exactly the infrastructure that does not exist and that privacy and political constraints make difficult to build.

title: Restitution Exchange Ring — proposal
open: Can parties seeking restitution agree on exchanges of property without revealing what they are privately willing to accept? Formally, can mutually acceptable, disjoint exchange cycles be found among private acceptable alternatives without the process leaking those alternatives?
status: No such private mechanism exists yet: title transfer, physical access, and fair completion all require outside enforcement, and the outputs of proposals reveal preferences even when the search itself stays private. Related techniques come from private matching and malicious computation.
solved_when: A protocol produces disjoint, mutually acceptable exchange cycles while keeping each party's acceptable alternatives private — including privacy of preferences from the proposal outputs themselves.
why: It would let restitution packages be assembled without exposing bargaining positions or family histories, which is what currently deters participation.

title: Restitution Reversal Reserve — proposal
open: Can a restitution award be structured so that part of the payment is released immediately while a bounded "correction reserve" is held back, with later authorized decisions allowed to redirect only that reserved portion? Formally, the provisional award must embed the reserve as a bounded quantity, and no post-issuance decision may move funds beyond it.
status: Currently a proposal only. Handling of uncertainty and fraud is acknowledged to need a real process, and clocks, decision credentials, and escrow enforcement remain assumptions; the abort path may delay release. Related ideas draw on provisions and anonymous authorization credentials.
solved_when: A process exists in which a provisional award carries a bounded hidden correction reserve, and any later authorized decision provably redirects at most that reserved portion — with the remaining award irrevocably released.
why: It enables earlier payments to claimants while limiting future hardship from erroneous awards, since reversals are absorbed by the reserve rather than clawed back from recipients.

title: Century Baton — proposal
open: How can a long-lived archive transfer its secret shares among successive generations of custodians so that neither reconstruction of the secret nor a silent weakening of access rules ever occurs during the transition?
status: This is a proposal. The requirements identified are that secure erasure, institutional diversity, migration, and recoverable handover must persist through transfers, and that already compromised old ciphertexts cannot be rescued retrospectively. Related work includes archive secret redistribution and CHURP.
solved_when: A share-transfer protocol is specified in which secure erasure, institutional diversity, migration, and recoverable handover all persist across every generational change, without reconstruction of the archive secret and without weakening prior access rules; compromised old ciphertexts need not be rescued retrospectively.
why: It is what allows archives to outlive governments, religious administrations, and trustees — the custodians change, the evidence survives intact.

title: Constitution-Locked Archive Migration — proposal
open: When an archive's technological substrate must be replaced, how can we guarantee that the migration honors the disclosure boundaries the original contributors set — protecting inputs, recipients, query powers, repetition limits, and allowed failure or timing leakage? Formally, this asks for a migration procedure that provably refines the old disclosure behavior rather than merely reproducing its output distribution.
status: Equal output ranges are known to be insufficient as a substitute for refinement, and unrestricted program equivalence is unavailable. Semantic exposure through permitted prose remains difficult to control. Key works: proof-carrying data; archive share redistribution.
solved_when: A replacement mechanism exists whose disclosure behavior provably refines the original's protections over protected inputs, recipients, query powers, repetition limits, and the permitted failure and timing leakage — going beyond equality of output ranges.
why: Without such a refinement notion, every technological renewal of a long-lived archive risks silently eroding the terms under which contributors donated their evidence; with it, archives can be migrated across generations while the original boundaries remain binding.

title: Excerpt Passport — proposal
open: Can a party cite a protected archival record by publishing only an excerpt, together with a proof that the excerpt is an allowed transformation of the committed record — without revealing anything else about the full source?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The obstacle is that exact wording can identify a speaker, syntactic redaction does not establish semantic anonymity, and provenance is not truth — so any proof of allowed transformation must be paired with meaningful anonymity guarantees. Key works: proof-carrying data; zero-knowledge computation.
solved_when: A published excerpt exists alongside a verifiable proof (in the spirit of proof-carrying data or zero-knowledge computation) that it derives from the committed record via an allowed transformation, and the full record remains hidden from unrestricted inspection.
why: It would let historians and courts cite protected evidence persuasively while the underlying archive stays sealed, replacing trust in the archivist with a checkable artifact.

title: No Automatic Unsealing — proposal
open: Can an intergenerational archive be designed so that secrecy is never lifted automatically — so that access passes to a chosen successor only when authenticated succession conditions are met, while the default outcome of any ambiguity is to keep the archive sealed?
status: Death and succession are external facts that the system cannot observe, and no new consent can be inferred from the deceased; disputes and lost keys therefore require recovery procedures agreed upon in advance. Key works: threshold credentials; archive redistribution.
solved_when: A mechanism is specified in which the default transition preserves secrecy, and unsealing occurs only under authenticated, previously agreed succession conditions, including handling of disputes and lost keys via pre-agreed recovery procedures.
why: It would allow posthumous research to proceed within boundaries the contributor actually chose, rather than leaving consent to be inferred after death.

title: Hidden-Object Recovery Drill — proposal
open: Can an archive holder prove — without revealing any contents — that a hidden object remains recoverable at each fixed epoch, and trigger private repair tasks whenever redundancy falls below an assurance threshold?
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists. The extraction theorem must cover colluding stores, hidden challenges, and adaptive repair, and a passed audit guarantees neither future availability nor independent physical replicas. Related work includes Shacham–Waters retrievability proofs and archive redistribution.
solved_when: A retrievability-extraction theorem is established that covers colluding stores, hidden challenges, and adaptive repair, and the defined retrievability assurance is certified at every fixed epoch with repair issued when redundancy becomes insufficient.
why: It would allow detection and repair of archival decay in intergenerational archives without ever opening sensitive collections to inspectors or repairers.

title: Bounded Contradiction Map — proposal
open: Can an archive publish, in a machine-checkable form, the aggregate inconsistencies across its historical records — for example, pairs of sources asserting mutually exclusive date intervals — without exposing the underlying vulnerable sources?
status: This is currently only a proposal. Any design must respect that contradiction is not proof of lying — perspective, transcription, and uncertainty all matter — and omitted inputs must be represented as incomplete coverage. Key works: Malicious MPC; PINQ.
solved_when: A published artifact exists that expresses approved aggregate inconsistencies under formal predicates (e.g., mutually exclusive date intervals), where omitted inputs are represented as incomplete coverage rather than silence, so the result is checkable by machine.
why: It lets historians prioritize which disputed questions to investigate while keeping sensitive or vulnerable source material non-public.

title: Nonresetting Historical Privacy Budget — proposal
open: Can we design a privacy mechanism for archival records in which the cumulative disclosure budget never resets — persisting across replicas, successive researchers, changing policy versions, and generational handoffs — even as the underlying neighboring-dataset relation evolves with consent and linkage changes?
status: The core obstacle identified is that the evolving neighboring-dataset relation must handle consent and linkage changes, and that ordinary composition cannot repair a false identity-linkage model or erase prior outputs. Key works in this lineage include PINQ and CHURP.
solved_when: A formally specified mechanism exists under which the cumulative privacy budget is provably monotone and nonresetting across all axes named (replicas, researchers, policy versions, generations), and the analysis covers the evolving neighboring-dataset relation induced by consent and linkage changes rather than assuming it fixed.
why: It would let historical research proceed with formal privacy promises that survive administrative turnover; without it, each replica, new researcher, or policy revision silently restarts the budget, and composition cannot repair a false identity-linkage model or erase prior outputs.

title: Plural-Memory Invariant — proposal
open: For a predefined question, release unanimous support, absence of unanimity, or incomplete coverage across committed archival snapshots.
status: Agreement among selected records is not historical truth. Adaptive predicates can fingerprint dissenting archives; abstention must remain distinct from disagreement.
why: Shared statements alongside protected disagreement.

title: Treaty Readiness Barrier — proposal
open: Can a set of parties jointly certify that all ceasefire and return preconditions hold — and issue authorization for the next agreed civilian action — while revealing nothing about which parties were ready, in what order, or who (if anyone) held out?
status: No construction is known. The requirements stated so far: monitors must be accurate; a conjunction can reveal a holdout to colluders; and missing inputs and abort do not prove anyone was unready. Candidate technical ingredients are SPDZ-style MPC and threshold credential issuance.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which authenticated readiness conditions yield either a valid authorization for the next agreed civilian action or no authorization, with accuracy of the monitors guaranteed, and in which a conjunction never reveals a holdout to colluders, while missing inputs and aborts do not prove any party was unready.
why: It would let parties make coordinated reconstruction commitments without exposing who was ready first, removing an incentive obstacle to simultaneous demobilization and voluntary return.

title: Demobilization Count Without Roster — proposal
open: Can a demobilization program publish only authorized aggregate counts of distinct, voluntarily enrolled individuals — with each person privately proving they hold a current reintegration attestation — so that no central roster of participants ever needs to exist?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. Current practice leaves enrollment open to fabrication or misclassification, and any deployed scheme must protect endpoints and service cohorts while ensuring aborted accounting does not automatically suspend essential assistance. Related directions include Coconut (anonymous credentials) and private set matching.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which (i) only authorized aggregates of distinct voluntarily enrolled persons are released, (ii) each individual can privately prove their own eligibility via a current reintegration attestation, and (iii) endpoints and service cohorts remain protected, with an aborted accounting run not automatically suspending essential assistance.
why: It would allow funders and implementers to finance and verify reintegration without any broadly shared targeting register — a list whose disclosure or misuse can endanger former combatants.

title: Destruction Token Cancellation — proposal
open: Can a treaty accounting rule count uniquely committed destruction items — each carrying a valid, independently witnessed retirement certificate — without moving the sensitive inventries themselves? Formally, the question is to construct an accounting procedure that aggregates these certificates into a verifiable total of distinct retired items.
status: This is a proposal; inspectors currently must establish physical retirement directly. The existing proof covers declared items only and cannot establish that undeclared inventory does not exist.
solved_when: A procedure exists that counts exactly the unique committed items carrying valid independently witnessed retirement certificates, producing bounded compliance evidence without transferring sensitive inventories.
why: It gives inspectors bounded, verifiable compliance evidence while the physical items and sensitive inventories stay in place.

title: Homecoming Capacity Match — proposal
open: Can a matchmaking protocol be built that lets displaced families privately state their preferences and service providers privately state their authenticated housing or service capacities, so that each family receives an individually encrypted offer that is feasible on both sides, without exposing preferences or capacities to anyone?
status: The core gap identified is that arithmetic feasibility is not physical safety: matching may compute correctly yet still leak identity through rare requirements, and revocability before acceptance plus abort-without-obligation must hold alongside privacy. Key works referenced are malicious MPC and private matching; no protocol meeting these safety conditions is recorded.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which arithmetic feasibility of every matched offer is verified against authenticated capacities, preferences remain revocable at any point before acceptance, no rare requirement can be leveraged to identify a family, and an abort produces no relocation obligation for any party.
why: It enables return and reintegration planning without public maps of intended return, which would otherwise endanger the very families the planning is meant to serve.

title: Reciprocal Return Option — proposal
open: Can return options be designed so that a household's reserved place is activated only while consent continues and local readiness is independently attested, and lapses automatically otherwise?
status: Readiness indicators cannot guarantee safety; scarcity allocation and cancellation still need agreed rules, and observers may still detect activation.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which reservation activation requires both ongoing household consent and independently attested local readiness, with agreed rules for scarcity allocation and cancellation, and where the option otherwise expires.
why: It enables reversible planning instead of public promises people may fear to withdraw.
key_works: Anonymous credentials; MPC over private state.

title: Return-Neutral Aid Proof — proposal
open: Can a committed policy, facing participants whose circumstances are hidden, be made to provably deliver identical named benefits whether a person stays or returns?
status: As proposed, encoded equality cannot prevent intimidation, discretionary denial, or manipulated background attributes; it does not establish the policy's overall fairness.
solved_when: A scheme is given that certifies equality of the named benefits under "stay" and "return" for the committed policy, robust to the hidden circumstances of participants.
why: It provides a checkable boundary against conditioning essential assistance on departure.

title: Civilian Peace Dividend — proposal
open: Can a committed funding pool be made to pay out to agreed civilian beneficiaries exactly when authenticated indicators cross predetermined thresholds, without any individual monitor's report ever being revealed? Formally, the goal is a construction combining conditional release of pooled funds with privacy of the underlying monitor reports.
status: No construction exists yet. Known obstacles are that metrics can distort behavior and that monitors can be biased; any design must also guarantee that escrow exists and that essential aid stays outside the conditional pool, including during abort. Key works: SPDZ; Provisions.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which payouts occur precisely when authenticated indicators meet the predetermined thresholds, individual monitor reports are withheld from all parties, the escrow pool is actually committed (funds exist before thresholds are evaluated), and essential aid remains outside the conditional pool at all times, including during an abort.
why: It lets civilian beneficiaries and funders share incentives for verified progress on ceasefire, demobilization, and return conditions while avoiding the concentration of sensitive monitoring data in any single hands.

title: Emergency-Power Expiry Seal — proposal
open: How can exceptional access or inspection capabilities be designed so that they become invalid at a fixed deadline, with renewal requiring fresh authorization, while ordinary entitlements retain separate rules?
status: This is a proposal. Known limitations: verifiers and clocks must enforce expiry, and cryptography cannot compel relinquishment of physical power or prevent institutional bypass.
solved_when: A construction exists in which verifiers and clocks enforce expiry of exceptional capabilities at the fixed deadline, renewal is impossible without fresh authorization, and ordinary entitlements operate under separate rules unaffected by the exceptional-expiry mechanism.
why: It prevents temporary technical powers from persisting merely through procedural deadlock, ensuring emergency authority lapses rather than ossifying.

title: Blind Basin Compact — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can communities sharing a water basin compute fair individual quotas — from private forecasts, minimum-service commitments, and demand curves — without any custodian trusted with everyone's data, while producing a public proof that the quota computation was carried out correctly?
status: Sensors and forecasts can fail, and upstream actors can ignore quotas; the certificate establishes only correct model execution, while credible measurement and physical enforcement remain external. Key works: secure economic mechanisms; malicious MPC.
solved_when: A protocol exists that takes private forecasts, minimum-service commitments, and demand curves as inputs and outputs individual quotas together with a publicly verifiable conservation proof, with no party trusted with all communities' private inputs.
why: It enables water-sharing agreements in settings where no operator is trusted with every community's vulnerabilities, decoupling the allocation computation itself from the need for a central trusted custodian.

title: Grid Truce Dispatch — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can mutually distrusting grid operators jointly dispatch power — authorizing boundary flows and local control actions — while producing a common, verifiable proof that the dispatch complies with the committed network approximation and reserve requirements, without any operator learning more than its authorized share?
status: A simplified model does not guarantee physical stability. Telemetry, model-error margins, and independent protection systems require engineering beyond cryptography. Relevant techniques include malicious MPC and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which operators learn only authorized boundary flows and local actions, and all parties obtain a shared proof of compliance with the committed electrical approximation and reserves; the protocol's guarantees must account for the simplified model's failure to ensure physical stability.
why: It would let civilian electrical systems cooperate across trust boundaries without exposing operational weaknesses such as telemetry details, model errors, or protection configurations.

title: Unadvertised Rescue Capacity — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can medical institutions cooperate on patient transfers and rescue capacity without any trusted operator, when each is unwilling to reveal its regional inventories or unmatched requests? Specifically, can private capacity offers and minimal authorized clinical requirements be combined to produce patient-specific destinations while withholding all other information — regional inventories, unmatched requests — even from receiving clinicians, except for what care necessarily requires?
status: No construction exists yet; this is a proposal. The obstacles on record are that capacity changes rapidly, clinical suitability requires judgment, and inputs can be false, while receiving clinicians necessarily learn information needed for care. Relevant primitives are private-output MPC and selective-disclosure credentials.
solved_when: A protocol exists that takes private capacity offers and minimal authorized clinical requirements as inputs and outputs patient-specific destinations, while provably revealing nothing beyond what receiving clinicians need for care — even when inputs are false and capacity changes rapidly.
why: It would let communities that fear exposing scarcity or surplus still coordinate medical rescue, unlocking cooperation that is currently blocked by mutual distrust.

title: Reciprocal Public-Good Trigger — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can a group provision a shared public good — funding it only when the total raised meets a target and each constituency contributes at least its floor — without any participant learning who donated or how much any constituency gave in total?
status: Refundable escrow and payment finality currently require additional assumptions; strategic withholding and artificial constituency splitting remain to be addressed by incentive analysis. Key works: MPC economic mechanisms; Coconut.
solved_when: A mechanism exists that executes pledges exactly when both the overall funding target and all constituency floors are met, with donor identities and constituency totals withheld, under explicit and checkable assumptions for refundable escrow and payment finality, and with an incentive analysis ruling out strategic withholding and artificial constituency splitting.
why: It would let joint ventures such as schools, sanitation projects, or restoration efforts be funded without a trusted fundraiser, replacing that trust with cryptography.

title: No-Pricelist Procurement — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can a group of buyers jointly procure a common good through multiparty computation such that each participant learns only the winning contract and its own allocation and invoice, while losing bids and rivals' demand curves remain hidden?
status: Goods and delivery require outside verification. The chosen pricing rule may reveal a rival's demand through a buyer's own bill, so the payment rule itself is a leakage channel that must be addressed. Key work: *Multiparty Computation Goes Live*.
solved_when: A procurement protocol is designed in which the outputs are exactly the selected contract and each buyer's own allocation and invoice; no party, including the operator of the computation, learns losing bids or any other buyer's demand curve.
why: It enables collective purchasing — pooling demand for better terms — without any institution exposing to rivals how much it depends on the good or what it is willing to pay.

title: Private Burden Ceiling — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can a group fund shared infrastructure so that each party's cost share is verifiably below a privately evidenced affordability cap, while still satisfying an agreed funding rule? Formally, this asks for a mechanism — likely combining secure computation with collaborative proofs — that certifies the burden constraint holds without exposing parties' private financial information.
status: Current approaches fall short: attestations may omit resources, declared outside options can be strategic, and accounting predicates do not establish actual hardship. Relevant lines of work include private economic MPC and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A construction is given in which cost shares provably satisfy the agreed funding rule and each party's share remains below its privately evidenced affordability cap, with no party's private financial data revealed beyond what the protocol itself establishes.
why: It would let communities with mutual financial distrust still build shared flood-control, sewage, or restoration projects, by replacing trust in each other's claimed hardship with cryptographic verification.

title: Compatibility Without Inventory — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can a set of mutually suspicious operators jointly select a configuration that satisfies all of their committed interoperability constraints, without any operator learning which options were rejected or being able to attribute specific incompatibilities to other participants?
status: This is a proposal-stage problem. Currently, formal compatibility determination still requires physical integration tests, and stale inventories and repeated queries can expose or fingerprint equipment. Related technical directions include malicious-secure MPC and collaborative zk-SNARKs.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which the parties converge on a configuration satisfying every committed constraint, while (i) no party learns anything about rejected options beyond what its own inputs and the final choice reveal, and (ii) no party can attribute an incompatibility to a particular other party. No round, size, or budget targets are specified; the natural criterion for this problem type is information-theoretic or cryptographic privacy alongside correctness of the selected configuration.
why: It would let operators share warning, humanitarian-communications, and utility interfaces across organizations that do not trust a common operator, where today stale inventories and repeated queries can expose or fingerprint equipment.

title: Silent Externality Settlement — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Can parties who impose externalities on each other — pollution, resource depletion, noise — settle charges and credits without any trusted operator, using only authenticated measurements? Ideally, a protocol in which bounded, signed measurements are converted into private charges or credits, while producing public proof that the agreed settlement formula was applied and the accounting balances.
status: Currently only a proposal. Signed measurements alone can be false, strategically placed, or incomplete, and attribution and enforcement require agreement reached outside the circuit. Related primitives come from Prio and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A protocol exists that takes authenticated bounded measurements as input and outputs private per-party charges or credits, together with a public proof that the agreed formula was correctly applied and that the accounts balance.
why: It would let environmental compacts function among mutually distrusting parties, with no centralized industrial intelligence gathering measurements or adjudicating disputes.

title: Coalition-Cut Compiler — proposal
open: Can we build a compiler that, given a declared set of possible coalitions, a network model, and a specification of outputs, derives the conditions under which the protocol achieves confidentiality, correctness with abort, authorization, and achievable delivery? In other words, it should determine when a given coalition structure is compatible with secure multi-party computation under the stated network assumptions.
status: This is a proposal. Currently, representing an access structure does not establish robust MPC, and cryptography cannot discover hidden common ownership or make a declared coalition model true. Related foundations include span-program MPC and Canetti's UC framework.
solved_when: A construction exists that takes as input a coalition model, network model, and output specification, and produces provable conditions characterizing confidentiality, correctness with abort, authorization, and delivery for that setting.
why: It would yield treaties and protocol agreements that explicitly display which alliances could compromise them, rather than leaving coalition structure implicit and unexamined.

title: Refusal-Aware Privacy Ledger — proposal
open: Can we build a disclosure ledger that tracks every privacy event — acceptances, refusals, timing classifications, and released outputs — across related protocols, and gates each new query on that full history?
status: The target must compose selective abort and adaptive cross-protocol queries, and it does not circumvent fairness impossibility. Key works include privacy filters, UC security, and Cleve.
solved_when: A ledger mechanism exists that composes selective abort with adaptive cross-protocol queries, correctly accounting for acceptance, refusal, timing classes, and released outputs before permitting further queries.
why: Institutions cannot reset disclosure budgets by relabeling failed attempts; without such a ledger, aborted queries would silently escape privacy accounting.

title: Witness-Safe Fault Proof — proposal
open: Can a fault proof name the culpable institutional key and the rule it violated, while keeping hidden which record and which session within a fixed batch the fault concerned? Formally, the proof must establish blame and the violated rule without revealing the record/session location beyond the batch bound.
status: Non-framing and selective-abort privacy remain unproven. A deliberately unique fault can identify its victim despite ZK, and timeouts require network assumptions before implying blame. Related directions include provable selective-abort identification and collaborative proofs.
solved_when: A proof exists that is non-framing and preserves selective-abort privacy: it identifies the culpable key and violated rule, and leaks nothing about the specific record or session within the fixed batch; handling of timeouts is analyzed under stated network assumptions.
why: It delivers public fault accountability without automatically producing witness-location evidence, so institutions can be held to rules without exposing which records or sessions were involved.

title: Interpreter Pluralism Pact — proposal
open: Independent implementations must prove conformity to the same bounded treaty semantics and numeric conventions.
status: Functionally equivalent circuits do not necessarily interoperate. Translation validation, backend interoperability, and overflow behavior require verification; matching code hashes are insufficient.
why: Cooperation without a shared vendor or opaque reference executable.

title: Cross-Treaty Identity Firewall — proposal
open: Can a person's entitlements — census, voting, lineage, and testimony — be issued and used under separate treaties so that no linkage is possible across purposes, except when a join is expressly authorized?
status: This is a proposal; the proof obligations — covering malicious issuers, chosen schemas, shared recovery, and lifetime composition — are stated but not discharged. Physical observations remain outside cryptographic unlinkability. Suggested foundations include Coconut and universally composable security.
solved_when: A construction and proof exist that establish unlinkability across purposes even in the presence of malicious issuers, chosen schemas, shared recovery mechanisms, and lifetime composition; physical observations remain outside the cryptographic guarantee.
why: A claimant seeking restitution would not thereby build a searchable political or testimonial profile about themselves.

title: Assumption-Diversity Covenant — proposal
open: Can we build a cryptographic construction that preserves its advertised secrecy whenever at least two of three designated candidate assumptions remain secure for the required parties under the declared failure model?
status: Known OT combiner results do not protect the whole stack; distinct assumptions need not fail independently, and unrestricted one-of-two black-box robustness cannot be presumed. Related work exists in robust-combiner research.
solved_when: A construction exists whose secrecy holds whenever any 2 of the 3 designated assumptions remain unbroken for the required parties under the declared failure model, with no reliance on unrestricted one-of-two black-box robustness.
why: It would yield long-lived agreements whose security does not hinge on a single mathematical foundation, surviving the failure of any one underlying assumption.

title: Victim-Selectable Everlasting Exit — proposal
open: Can a party permanently and selectively withdraw its data from an ongoing computation — even against a coalition that later captures all institutions and archived transcripts — such that the computation continues correctly on the remaining inputs while the withdrawing party retains a simulatable view? Formally, after deletion certificates verify, continuing computation must exclude the selected record, and the post-exit view must be simulatable from surviving inputs and permitted prior outputs.
status: The underlying tools exist: everlasting security transfer and deletion composition are established, drawing on certified-deletion computation and secret sharing. The open extension is efficient selective withdrawal in the presence of shared state and changing committees, where deletion can be refused.
solved_when: A construction is given in which, once required deletion certificates verify, the selected record is excluded from continuing computation and the post-exit view is simulatable from surviving inputs and permitted prior outputs — and the construction remains efficient under shared state and changing committees, including when deletion is refused.
why: It would provide a concrete route toward confidentiality that survives later institutional capture, where all present-day authorities and archives may turn hostile to the withdrawn record.

title: Treaty Continuation Without Replay — proposal
open: Can a long-running treaty-style protocol, after a crash or wholesale replacement of its operators, be restarted from a single committed history such that it provably continues from exactly that point — preserving accepted inputs, consumed permissions, and already released outputs — while rejecting any party's attempt to resume from an alternate history?
status: Recovery must account for early outputs, stale shares, and unavailable parties, and preserving privacy alone does not guarantee progress. Related foundations include UC security and proactive secret sharing.
solved_when: A recovery mechanism exists that restarts from one committed history, preserves accepted inputs, consumed permissions, and already released outputs, and rejects alternate histories, while accounting for early outputs, stale shares, and unavailable parties.
why: It would let long proceedings survive crashes and operator replacement without duplicating benefits or disclosures — the difference between a durable agreement and one that must be replayed or trusted on faith after disruption.
